text:
kai: quick sync — planning to backfill console routing affinities for legacy v1 clients next week. want to avoid a surprise mass-switch when header negotiation falls back to server-side default. thoughts?

liam: +1. runtime needs to know whether to prefer sticky token routing or version header. current default is header > affinity > default-route. backfill would populate affinity for tokens we can map.

sasha: can we put a tenant-level opt-out in console? some customers requested explicit control. even a single toggle: 'honor console affinity' on/off.

olivia: we can add a toggle but UX needs to show impact. propose a small modal that explains: "Backfill will set routing affinity for historic tokens to preserve behavior; disabling keeps header-first routing." include a preview table (samples + percent of requests affected).

maya: important: quota implications. if affinities push traffic to older v1 pools, we might see hot shards and burst over reserved capacity. need smoothing window (e.g., 24h gradual ramp) or queue-based throttling for backfill application.

kai: agree re smoothing. idea: run backfill in cohorts — 1% per hour for 48h with telemetry checks and automated rollback if error-rate or latency spikes.

liam: runtime checklist: (1) accept affinity write with source=console-backfill tag, (2) respect a TTL override during ramp, (3) support dry-run mode where affinity is recorded but not used for routing. dry-run helps console preview.

olivia: dry-run + preview is exactly what UX needs. preview should show estimated percent of tenant traffic that would switch affinity and a sample list of token prefixes. simple graph: baseline route distribution vs post-backfill distribution.

sasha: +1. also we should show expected quota delta: "estimated additional v1 QPS" so account teams can pre-approve.

maya: on telemetry: we need three signals to gate progression: error-rate delta (5xxs), p99 latency delta, and quota pressure (reserved GPU utilization). if any exceed thresholds, the cohort halts and console notifies owner.

liam: implementable. add a small flag to routing policy: "affinity_source_priority": ["header", "affinity_console_backfill", "affinity_runtime", "fallback_route"]. that way console-tagged affinities can be bumped or deprioritized later without touching client headers.

kai: what about deprecation messaging? we still need to tell tenants on v1 that console-affinity may route them to v1 variants. need a banner in console and email for those on v1.

olivia: I'll add a banner and an admin email template. banner copy: "We're applying routing affinities to preserve current behavior for v1 clients. Learn more [link]." link -> docs page with rollback steps.

sasha: also expose an API for tenants to opt-in programmatically (for infra customers). console toggle should call that API.

liam: runtime: please ensure we log an event when affinity applied with tag, e.g., `affinity.apply(source=console-backfill, cohort=17, method=cohort-ramp)`. that enables us to query by cohort in traces.

maya: add metric `routing.affinity.backfill.create` with labels: tenant_id, cohort, prior_route, new_route. and alert rule if any tenant sees >20% increase in v1 route traffic in <1h.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/console-backfill-preview -> staging at 2026-03-22T02:10Z :rocket:

kai: owner matrix: olivia (console UX + rollout UI), liam (runtime changes + logging), maya (quota safety + telemetry), sasha (product + comms). I'll draft the rollout plan doc with cohort sizes and threshold numbers.

olivia: will prototype preview UI tomorrow, will attach screenshot to the rollout doc.

liam: I'll add dry-run and cohort metadata to affinity API by EOD.

maya: I'll propose thresholds: error-rate delta 0.5% absolute or 25% relative (whichever smaller), p99 latency +30ms absolute, reserved GPU util +10%. send PR for alerts.

kai: perfect. next sync Fri 11am PT. tagging @sasha for comms plan and @ops for post-deploy monitoring. :thumbsup:
